summary: Horry County tower on the SC Forestry Commission list; the Forest Lookouts page has only the county and agency. No source describes it or the site today.

facts.status_note: No source read says whether the tower still stands, or when it was built or taken down.

evidence.supports: Most operators from the 1960s on were women, often married to firefighters (statewide)
evidence.quote: From the 1960s on, most South Carolina tower operators were women; frequently their husbands were employed as firefighters.
In many cases, the tower became a family tradition, with adult children succeeding their parents as tower operators.

notes_for_editor: Thinnest of the three. The Aynor page on Forest Lookouts has only a header with the county and agency, and the state index repeats that line. No dated or described Aynor tower turned up in two searches. NHLR's South Carolina index in the cache has no Aynor entry. A Waymarking page for a Horry County fire tower on S.C. Highway 544 southeast of Conway came up in search, but it was not opened for content and is not evidence about Aynor; check whether it is the same site before linking. Brief's status, height and design stay unknown. Two searches and about three page reads.
